title: Finite stalk detection and Frobenius compatibility for lisse global sections
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a lisse $\Omega$-Weil sheaf, with lisse understood in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and Weil structure in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)$ be ordinary global sections and let $T$ be the geometric Frobenius induced by its Weil structure, as in [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. There is a finite family of closed points $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ of $Y_0$, not necessarily distinct, with geometric lifts $\bar y_i$ to $Y$ (distinct indices may carry the same closed point with different lifts), such that the evaluation map
$$A\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal G_{\bar y_i}$$
is injective. In particular $A$ is finite-dimensional over $\Omega$, and $T$ is a linear automorphism. The empty family is permitted for $Y=\varnothing$. For every closed point $y$ of $Y_0$ and chosen geometric lift $\bar y$, put $d=[\kappa(y):k_0]\ge1$. With $F_y$ the local geometric Frobenius [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], evaluation satisfies
$$\operatorname{ev}_{\bar y}(T^d a)=F_y\bigl(\operatorname{ev}_{\bar y}(a)\bigr)\quad(a\in A).$$

source.place: Second paragraph, closed-point Frobenius comparison, generalized from one connected component to finite stalk detection; project source: WeilConjectures/WeilSheaf/Stalk.lean, exists_injective_globalSectionsToStalkObj and finiteDimensional_globalSections (lines 383-468); WeilConjectures/WeilSheaf/StalkFrobeniusPow.lean, globalSectionsToStalkAt_comp_frobeniusEnd_pow (lines 215-235).

proof.text: By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $Y$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. A field is Noetherian, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] its underlying space is Noetherian: a strictly descending chain of closed sets would have no minimal member, contrary to that statement. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open] to obtain finitely many nonempty open connected components $C_1,\ldots,C_m$. Their complements are unions of the other open components, so each is also closed. Give each its open subscheme structure. Each $C_i$ is locally Noetherian by restriction to affine opens, quasi-compact because closed in $Y$, and separated by restriction of the diagonal. It is of finite type over $k$: its open immersion is locally of finite type and its source is quasi-compact. Thus each $C_i$ is Noetherian, separated, connected, and has $\ell$ invertible.

source.place: Tags 04MF, 04ME, 0052; finite-type/local-Noetherian input: morphisms.tex, Tags 01T4 and 01T6

proof.text: For each $C_i$, choose a closed point $z_i$ by [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point], since the underlying space of a scheme is Kolmogorov and $C_i$ is nonempty and quasi-compact. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $\kappa(z_i)$ is finite over the algebraically closed field $k$, hence equals $k$. This gives a $k$-point $\bar y_i:\operatorname{Spec}k\to C_i\subset Y$. If $y_i$ is its image in $Y_0$, the residue-field injection $\kappa(y_i)\hookrightarrow k$ makes $\kappa(y_i)$ algebraic over $k_0$. Its transcendence degree is zero, so [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), now on the finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, says that $y_i$ is closed. This chooses the required family; different $C_i$ may project to the same $y_i$. For $Y=\varnothing$ choose the empty family.

source.place: Tag 005E, lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point; residue fields: blueprint lem-kun-closed-point-field, clause (a)

proof.text: Both models of $\mathcal G$ are used, and they agree at a common finite stage $E$: by [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] the adic system $(\mathcal G_n)$ of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] gives the lisse $E_Y$-module $(\varprojlim_n\nu_Y^*\mathcal G_n)[1/\varpi]$, fully faithfully on the rationalized lisse category and compatibly with module pullback, and by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] this is the realization of the underlying lisse object of the heart, with units, pullbacks and point fibres $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*-)$ identified with $E_Y$, module pullback and sections at $s$. Sections at $s$ of $\bar x^*\varprojlim_n\nu^*\mathcal G_n$ are $\varprojlim_n(\mathcal G_n)_{\bar x}$, so the fibres agree with those of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and $A$ is the same in both models. On $C_i$ the fibre functor at $\bar y_i$ is faithful by [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2). Its hypotheses hold by step 1: $C_i$ is connected, Noetherian, separated, and $\ell$ is invertible. A section $a_i$ of $\mathcal G|_{C_i}$ is the morphism $u_{a_i}:\underline\Omega_{C_i}\to\mathcal G|_{C_i}$ sending $1$ to $a_i$. The unit is lisse and its fibre is $\Omega$, by that same tensor equivalence. If $a_i$ evaluates to zero at $\bar y_i$, the fibre of $u_{a_i}$ sends $1$ to zero and is the zero linear map. Faithfulness implies $u_{a_i}=0$, hence $a_i=0$. A section of $Y$ whose evaluations all vanish therefore vanishes on every member of the open covering $(C_i)$ and is zero by the sheaf axiom. Applying this to the difference of two sections proves injectivity of the displayed evaluation map.

source.place: (1.1.6), p. 150, fibre equivalence; agent application of its faithfulness to morphisms from the unit

proof.text: The fibres $\mathcal G_{\bar y_i}$ are finite-dimensional by the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ clause of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2). Thus the finite product in step 3 has dimension $N=\sum_i\dim_\Omega\mathcal G_{\bar y_i}$. An injective linear map carries linearly independent vectors to linearly independent vectors, so $A$ has dimension at most $N$. For the empty family this says $A=0$.

Sections as unit morphisms, and the point transport on them. On sections: $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is an equivalence with $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\mathbf 1_s)=\Omega$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], so $\mathrm H^0\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf 1_s,N)$; transposing along $La_Y^*\dashv Ra_{Y*}$ with its triangle identities [fix-prop-adjunctions](1), and the unit identification $La_Y^*\mathbf 1_s\cong\mathbf 1_Y$ of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], gives $H^0(Y,\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf 1_Y,\mathcal G)=A$ (step 3). For $w:\mathbf 1_s\to N$, naturality [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2) gives $\iota_N(w(1))=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*w)(\iota_{\mathbf 1_s}(1))$, and $\iota_{\mathbf 1_s}(1)=1$ since restriction and insertion in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] keep the constant section; so on $H^0$, $\iota$ is $w\mapsto Lg_s^*w$ composed with the unit comparison. Steps 6 and 9 use these two identifications.

source.place: (1.1.7) and (1.1.12), pp. 151-152: fibre at the geometric point of Spec k and sections; reviewer repair making the H^0 and point-transport identifications explicit

proof.text: Write $g=g_Y$, $h=g_s$, $P=g^*$ on lisse sheaves, and $\theta:P\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G$. We use actual section pullback, including its unit comparison: for $v:\underline\Omega_Y\to\mathcal G$, write $P(v)$ for $P(v)\circ(\underline\Omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}P\underline\Omega_Y)$. By step 5, the ordinary transport $\tau$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] sends the section $v$ to this section $P(v)$. Here is the adjunction calculation specifying the map: substitute the unit--square-comparison--counit formula of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1) into $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*})\iota$; after transposition, the adjacent unit and counit cancel by the triangular identity, leaving pullback of $v$ along $g$ and the constant-unit comparison. This calculation is an identity of the specified derived system maps, by the mate-pasting assertion of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; it is not an inference from equality of all finite reductions. For lisse objects, [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies these pullbacks, units, tensors and point transports with the ordinary module-sheaf maps, compatibly with composition and coefficient extension. Localizing the same system identity and passing to a common finite coefficient-field stage therefore gives it at $\Omega$. Finally [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] gives the concrete formula $T(v)=\theta\circ P(v)$.

source.place: (1.1.10), pp. 151-152, and (1.1.14), p. 153; agent expansion of transport on a section using the specified exchange mate

proof.text:
Iterate the formula of step 6. With the canonical composition identifications, put $\theta^{[1]}=\theta$ and $\theta^{[r+1]}=\theta^{[r]}\circ(g^r)^*\theta$, as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Then
$$T^r(v)=\theta^{[r]}\circ(g^r)^*v\quad(r\ge1).$$
For $r=1$ this is step 6. For the induction step, compose the expression for $T^r$ with the expression for $T$ and use functoriality of pullback:
$$\theta^{[r]}(g^r)^*(\theta\,g^*v)=\theta^{[r]}(g^r)^*\theta\,(g^{r+1})^*v=\theta^{[r+1]}(g^{r+1})^*v.$$
The unit comparisons are preserved by composition by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. This calculation takes place at a common field stage for the finitely many morphisms involved; it does not require a lattice preserved by $\theta$.

source.place: (1.1.10), pp. 151-152; iterated Weil structure as in def-weil-local-frobenius-trace

proof.text: The transport $\tau_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso](3), at $\Lambda=\Omega$. The Weil structure $\theta$ is an isomorphism; applying ordinary cohomology to it preserves invertibility. Hence [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] expresses $T$ on $H^0=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)$ as a composite of two linear isomorphisms. This proves that $T$ is an automorphism, also when $A=0$.

source.place: (1.1.10) and (1.1.14), pp. 151-153; invertibility of the two factors of the specified global operator

proof.text:
Fix any closed $y$, its chosen lift $z=\bar y$, and $d=[\kappa(y):k_0]\ge1$. In the notation of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], $g^dz=zh^d$. Put $N=z^*\mathcal G$ and let $b:(h^d)^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*(g^d)^*\mathcal G$ be the composition comparison associated to this equality. Evaluating a section $v$ means applying $z^*v$ to $1$ in the constant point fibre. The point transport $I^{[d]}$ sends this $1$ to $1$: each restriction and inverse-image insertion in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] preserves the constant unit section. Naturality of the point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), iterated $d$ times, consequently gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_z^{(g^d)^*\mathcal G}((g^d)^*v)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(b)I_N^{[d]}(\operatorname{ev}_z^{\mathcal G}(v)).$$
Indeed both sides are the fibre of $(zh^d)^*v=(g^dz)^*v$ applied to the transported $1$; the composition and point-fibre identifications are precisely those preserved by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. Now evaluate step 7, using that evaluation of $\theta^{[d]}\circ(g^d)^*v$ is $\operatorname{Fib}_s(z^*\theta^{[d]})$ applied to the left side. The result is
$$\operatorname{ev}_z(T^dv)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(z^*\theta^{[d]})\operatorname{Fib}_s(b)I_N^{[d]}(\operatorname{ev}_z(v))=F_y(\operatorname{ev}_z(v)),$$
where the last equality is exactly the defining composite of $F_y$ in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. This uses the semilinear return $g^dz=zh^d$, not $g^dz=z$.
